supersedes.reason: Independent review reproduced delete-crash data loss, unstable put publication and commit ambiguity, references to unavailable objects, a rights-transition read bypass, false quarantine during active reads, and unbounded hostile metadata types. This manifest records the focused consistency remediation.

checks.result: All 45 task-risk tests pass. The focused regressions cover pre- and post-COMMIT delete crashes, failed restore retry, held put bytes, late write/replace/hardlink attempts, lost COMMIT acknowledgement, deleted/quarantined/pending document-link denial, rights-transition serialization, active-reader busy retry, and hostile non-string metadata.

Formatting, Ruff, and mypy pass for all 98 governed Python files. Architecture passes for the private object-store/repository adapters and dependency-neutral ports. Diff-aware ADR enforcement passes with 15 records and 27 changed paths. Quality-report SHA-256: 18bf2de2032ab9d7325c5919e63549d2e421b03f06e97a0719f158acd706ab01.

All six runnable focused packaging tests pass with one Windows-token symlink skip. evidence: Put retains the exact verified, write/delete-denying file handle through definitive SQLite metadata publication. It validates single-link identity before and after COMMIT; a late hardlink advances the committed row to quarantined instead of returning available bytes, while write and replacement attempts are denied.

A COMMIT that succeeds but loses its acknowledgement is reconciled through a fresh canonical metadata read while the exact file remains held. Exact committed metadata returns the available projection and the new file is never removed; an absent row permits cleanup only after the held reader closes.

Delete stages bytes at a deterministic project-opaque recovery identity. Restart verifies and restores exact bytes when metadata remained available/quarantined, removes them only when deletion committed, and retains the recovery artifact when restore itself fails so a later restart can retry.

Open reserves current metadata before verification and transfers both the guarded SQLite transaction and exact verified reader into the controlled stream. Rights/state writers cannot overtake plaintext use; local active-reader deletion returns RO-CORE-OBJECT-BUSY without quarantining intact bytes.

The canonical repository transaction checks that a non-null document object reference is currently available before inserting any immutable revision, document, provenance, or outbox fact. Pending, quarantined, deleted, and missing objects fail atomically; an available object remains linkable.

Seventeen direct object-store tests now include the six independent-review attack classes alongside prior streaming, deduplication, project-scope, corruption, staging-alias, restart, reference-count, and rollback coverage.

The reserved metadata transaction serializes rights and storage-state transitions for the held stream. A real concurrent writer remains blocked through verification and reading, then commits after stream close; the next open denies access.
Both hostile integer media_type and protection_profile values produce bounded ObjectStoreProblem outcomes with no retained cause or context.

The strict project-object-store-v1 profile now machine-binds held-handle publication, COMMIT-ack reconciliation, delete crash recovery, reserved access serialization, active-reader retry, and available-only document linkage.

The architecture guide describes the exact pre-/post-COMMIT recovery protocol and the T01 bounded reader serialization seam while retaining T02 authenticated-encryption and T03 full lease/quota/GC ownership.
The real frozen Core package contains the remediated object-store, repository, storage, and port modules; no UI or approved UI-reference bytes changed.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: The remediation changes destructive object deletion, filesystem/SQLite commit coupling, rights authorization, repository reference integrity, a low-level transferable guarded connection, strict portable policy, and frozen sidecar bytes. Verification therefore replays every prior finding, the adjacent late alias/state boundaries, all affected storage/schema/repository/architecture contracts, all governed Python quality, clean build identity, and one real Pythonless package build.
